claims.text: A refractory Mo-Nb-Ta-W high-entropy alloy can catalyze both HER and HOR effectively.
The refractory HEA will show lower overpotentials than standard Pt-based catalysts in acidic environments.
The refractory HEA will have greater durability than standard Pt-based catalysts in acidic environments.
The proposed starting material is equiatomic MoNbTaW.
Spark plasma sintering can produce a predominantly single-phase bcc MoNbTaW alloy.
Acid etching and annealing expose a high-entropy catalytic surface.
Lattice distortion and multi-element mixing in the bcc HEA modify its surface electronic states.
Lattice distortion and multi-element mixing increase the number of active sites for hydrogen adsorption.
Lattice distortion shifts the HEA d-band center to an optimal position.
The proposed d-band-center shift balances hydrogen adsorption and desorption.
The multi-principal-element composition increases resistance to surface poisoning.
The multi-principal-element composition increases resistance to dissolution.
Balanced hydrogen adsorption and desorption promote HER and HOR activity.
Resistance to poisoning and dissolution enhances durability during HER and HOR.
The HEA electrode will exhibit lower onset overpotentials for HER and HOR than a conventional Pt electrode under identical conditions.
The HEA electrode will exhibit lower Tafel slopes for HER and HOR than a conventional Pt electrode under identical conditions.
The HEA electrode will sustain catalytic performance over extended cycling better than a conventional Pt electrode.
The predicted enhancement is limited to acidic environments at ambient temperature.
The performance trend may differ in alkaline media or after substantially different surface treatments.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and predicted outcome specifically require lower overpotentials than Pt, but the falsification rule accepts merely comparable overpotentials, so a result that fails the stated improvement claim may nevertheless be treated as non-falsifying.
